Discrete-Time Intensity of Hitting Down

Source: R/04_dti.R
dti.Rd

Compute the probability of an operational-to-down transition at a given positive time in a finite-state Markov chain.

Usage

dti(x, time, up)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A nonempty positive integer vector of discrete time points, each less than .Machine$integer.max. Missing and infinite values are not allowed.

up

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length and order as time containing the discrete-time intensities.

Details

Equation (48) of Gavrilopoulos, Trevezas, and Votsi (2026) gives $$r(t) = \Pr(X_{t-1}\in U, X_t\in D) = a P^{t-1} J_U P e_D, \qquad t\geq1,$$ where \(U\) is the operational set, \(D\) its complement, \(J_U\) is the diagonal operational-state indicator matrix, and \(e_D\) is the down-state indicator vector. The full transition matrix evolves the initial distribution to time \(t-1\); paths may have failed and recovered before that time. This differs from the first-entry probability returned by ftp(). Paths starting down can contribute after recovery. The initial distribution is fixed and is not renormalized.

The vector \(J_U P e_D\) is computed by summing down-transition probabilities directly and setting its down-state entries to zero. Powers are computed once by Ppowers(). Empty and full operational sets give zero intensity.

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161.

See also

ftp(), avail(), vcov_dti()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
dti(x, time = 1:3, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.08 0.10 0.11
vcov_dti(x, time = 3L, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.05826667
